title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident illustrates a deliberate attempt to manipulate AI systems at the data-ingestion stage rather than at the point of model inference. A fictitious organisation with no physical presence, no named staff, and no genuine research capacity produced an extraordinary volume of text in a very short time using a platform explicitly designed to optimize content for AI chatbots. The goal, as reported, was to place that content into the repositories from which AI training data is drawn, so that models such as ChatGPT and Claude would absorb and later reproduce its framing as if it were neutral academic analysis. The failure mode here is not a model hallucinating but a system being targeted for manipulation through its upstream data supply.

The operation registered as a foreign agent with the US Justice Department, which makes the funding relationship a matter of public record rather than allegation, but whether the content succeeded in entering any model's training data, and whether it measurably shifted any AI system's outputs, is not established by the reporting. The scale of production, over 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days, suggests the strategy depends on volume overwhelming the editorial and provenance checks that would normally filter training corpora. Catching this at the source would require training-data curators to verify the real-world existence and independence of cited institutions before including their output, a check that is not standard practice across the industry.

What is not established is whether any AI developer actually ingested this content, whether any model's responses were altered as a result, and whether the campaign constitutes illegal activity beyond the registered foreign-agent disclosure.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
An Israeli-funded fake think tank called the Hanover Institute published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days using a platform designed to optimize content for artificial intelligence chatbots. The nonexistent institute, which has no physical address or named staff, presents pro-Israel arguments on controversial topics including genocide allegations and Palestinian casualties, framing them as neutral academic research. The operation was registered with the US Justice Department as a foreign agent and is part of a broader campaign financed by tens of millions of dollars from the Israeli government routed through intermediaries including European advertising group Havas Media.

The campaign aims to influence how AI systems like ChatGPT and Claude present information about Israel by getting these materials into training data repositories. Israeli officials have reportedly expressed doubts about the strategy's effectiveness, with one official calling it a failure despite substantial spending. American public opinion has shifted significantly against Israel, with recent polls showing only 36% of Americans sympathize with Israel compared to Palestinians. Experts note that the approach treats Israel's political problems as marketing issues rather than addressing underlying policy concerns.
